cancelReturnsFunds.why: Jupiter builds cancel transactions from its own mainnet index, so an order created on a fork is unknown to it and the endpoint answers "Unable to cancel specified order", checked against the order this run created. Cancelling a fork order needs the instruction built against the Trigger program directly rather than through the API, which is the remaining work on this clause

depositMatchesAllowance.states: the vault deposit reduces the Swig allowance by exactly the deposit
depositMatchesAllowance.why: the allowance did not move at all: 500000000 before and after, against a deposit of 100000000. The order was signed by root, and root holds every action, so the deposit never passed the agent's cap. That is the honest answer to this clause and it is worth more than a pass: a Trigger order created by root moves funds the agent cap does not see. It is only safe because the agent cannot create one, which is this spike's other finding. Wallet balance moved -109597840 lamports over the same period, which is the deposit plus rent
